title: Industrial Revolution Begins
dramaticText: The machines awakened. Steam and steel promised progress, but the atmosphere began remembering every smokestack.
childPerspective: Children of this era watched the first smokestacks rise, unknowing that these tall towers would forever change the world.

events.title: Arrhenius Discovers Greenhouse Effect
events.description: Swedish scientist Svante Arrhenius first calculates how changes in atmospheric CO2 could affect Earth's temperature, laying the foundation for modern climate science.

events.title: Callendar Links CO2 to Warming
events.description: British engineer Guy Callendar publishes evidence showing that CO2 levels had increased and global temperatures were rising, connecting human activities to climate change.

events.title: Keeling Curve Begins
events.description: Charles David Keeling starts measuring atmospheric CO2 at Mauna Loa Observatory, establishing the longest continuous record of atmospheric CO2 concentration.

title: The Great Acceleration
dramaticText: We built a world of abundance, not knowing we were writing stories of scarcity for our children.
childPerspective: Baby boomers grew up believing progress meant prosperity, while their children would inherit a warming world.

events.title: Silent Spring Published
events.description: Rachel Carson's groundbreaking book exposes the environmental damage caused by pesticides, sparking the modern environmental movement.

events.title: Stockholm Conference
events.description: The first United Nations Conference on the Human Environment establishes environmental protection as a global priority.

events.title: IPCC Established
events.description: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change is created to assess scientific information related to climate change.

title: First Climate Signals
dramaticText: The Earth began to speak. Hurricanes grew stronger, glaciers retreated, but the world was still learning to listen.
childPerspective: Millennial children witnessed the first climate documentaries, learning their planet was in danger.

events.title: Kyoto Protocol Signed
events.description: International treaty commits developed nations to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, marking the first major global climate agreement.

events.title: An Inconvenient Truth
events.description: Al Gore's documentary brings climate change to mainstream audiences, winning an Academy Award and raising global awareness.

events.title: IPCC Nobel Peace Prize
events.description: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change shares the Nobel Peace Prize for efforts to build up and disseminate knowledge about climate change.

title: Climate Crisis Arrives
dramaticText: The future knocked on our door through smoke and flames. A generation stood up, refusing to inherit a broken world.
childPerspective: Gen Z children led school strikes, demanding adults act on climate change before it was too late.

events.title: Paris Agreement Signed
events.description: 195 countries commit to limiting global warming to well below 2°C, marking a historic moment in international climate cooperation.

events.title: Greta Thunberg's School Strike
events.description: A 15-year-old Swedish student begins weekly climate strikes outside Parliament, inspiring millions of young people worldwide.

events.title: Global Climate Strikes
events.description: Over 6 million people participate in climate strikes across 185 countries, making it the largest environmental protest in history.

title: The Crossroads Moment
dramaticText: This is our moment. The story of what happens next is still being written - through every choice we make today.
childPerspective: Today's children will live the consequences of our choices. Their future depends on the actions we take now.

events.title: COP26 Glasgow Summit
events.description: World leaders gather to accelerate action on climate change, with renewed commitments to net-zero emissions.

events.title: Renewable Energy Milestone
events.description: Global renewable energy capacity reaches record highs, with solar and wind becoming the cheapest energy sources.

events.title: Climate Justice Movement
events.description: Growing recognition of climate justice as communities worldwide demand equitable solutions to the climate crisis.
